copy.en:
Whose antennae are longer?

Crickets have long antennae, but grasshoppers have short ones — that's an easy way to tell them apart!
copy.tl:
Alin ang mas mahaba ang antena?

Mahaba ang antena ng kuliglig, pero maikli lang ang sa tipaklong — isa itong madaling paraan para makilala sila!
copy.bis:
Kinsa'y mas taas ang antena?

Taas ang antena sa kuliglig, apan mubo ra ang sa apan — usa kini ka sayon nga paagi aron mailhan sila!

assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a single molting event in a grasshopper, not a flow chart comparing life-cycle stages of animals. It does not support the competency's required activity or content.

copy.en: Right after a grasshopper molts, its new skin is soft and pale — and weak for a few hours until it hardens and gets its real color.
copy.tl: Pagkatapos magpalit-balat ang tipaklong, malambot at maputla muna ang bagong balat nito — mahina ito sa ilang oras hanggang tumigas at magkulay nang tama.
copy.bis: Human mag-molt ang apan, humok ug luspad una ang bag-o niining panit — maluya kini sulod sa pipila ka oras hangtod mogahi ug makuha ang husto nga kolor.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: a tympanum, a hearing organ, on either side of its abdomen that detects sound
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes an outer body part (tympanum) but its role is hearing, not moving or gathering food as required by the competency. It does not directly support the skill of identifying body parts' roles in movement or food gathering.

copy.en:
Where is a grasshopper's 'ear'?

Not on its head! A grasshopper has a tympanum, a hearing organ, on either side of its abdomen that detects sound.
copy.tl:
Saan matatagpuan ang 'tainga' ng tipaklong?

Hindi sa ulo ito naririnig! Mayroon itong tympanum, isang hearing organ, sa magkabilang tagiliran ng tiyan nito.
copy.bis:
Asa makit-an ang 'dalunggan' sa tipaklong?

Dili diay sa ulo kini nakadungog! Aduna kini tympanum, usa ka hearing organ, sa matag kilid sa iyang tiyan.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the grass is short and there are few trees

copy.en: A grassland looks flat and wide open because the grass is short and there are few trees — so you can see very far across it.
copy.tl: Mukhang patag at malawak ang grassland dahil mababa lang ang damo at kakaunti ang puno — kaya malayo ang naaabot ng iyong tingin.
copy.bis: Morag patag ug lapad ang grassland tungod kay mubo ra ang sagbot ug gamay ang kahoy — mao nga layo kaayo ang imong makita.

copy.en: A planet's surface gravity depends on its mass and its size!
copy.tl: Ang lakas ng grabidad sa ibabaw ng planeta ay nakadepende sa masa at laki nito!
copy.bis: Ang kusog sa grabidad sa ibabaw sa planeta nagdepende sa masa ug gidak-on niini!

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify gravity as a non-contact force that affects the behaviors of materials and objects on Earth in predictable ways
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions gravity but does not identify it as a non-contact force, nor does it discuss effects on objects on Earth. It only gives a comparative fact about the Moon's gravity, which is not the target concept of this competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The Moon's gravity is only about 1/6 of Earth's gravity

Why do you feel so light when you visit the Moon?

The Moon's gravity is only about 1/6 of Earth's gravity, so you feel much lighter there!
copy.tl:
Bakit mas magaan ang pakiramdam mo sa Buwan?

Ang gravity sa Buwan ay halos 1/6 lang ng gravity sa Earth, kaya mas magaan ka roon!
copy.bis:
Nganong mas gaan ka didto sa Bulan?

Ang gravity sa Bulan mga 1/6 lang sa gravity sa Earth, mao nga mas gaan ka didto!

copy.en: Of the four fundamental forces, gravity is the weakest — the strong nuclear force is the strongest!
copy.tl: Sa apat na pangunahing puwersa, ang gravity ang pinakamahina — ang strong nuclear force ang pinakamalakas!
copy.bis: Sa upat ka sukaranang puwersa, ang gravity mao ang kinahuyangan — ang strong nuclear force mao ang kinalig-onan!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Grazers eat grass on the ground, while browsers eat the leaves of taller plants and trees.

copy.en: Grazers eat grass on the ground, while browsers eat the leaves of taller plants and trees.
copy.tl: Ang mga grazer ay kumakain ng damo sa lupa, samantalang ang mga browser ay kumakain ng dahon ng matataas na halaman at puno.
copy.bis: Ang mga grazer nagakaon og sagbot sa yuta, samtang ang mga browser nagakaon sa mga dahon sa taas nga tanom ug kahoy.

assignedReviews.reason: The card identifies leaves and stems as edible parts but does not address their role in absorbing water and nutrients from the soil, which is the core of the competency.

copy.en: In leafy vegetables like pechay and kangkong, we eat the leaves and the tender stems.
copy.tl: Sa mga gulay na dahon tulad ng pechay at kangkong, ang dahon at malambot na tangkay ang kinakain natin.
copy.bis: Sa mga utanon nga dahon sama sa pechay ug kangkong, ang dahon ug humok nga tangkay ang atong gikaon.

copy.en: Some groundwater is trapped in a confined aquifer between tight rock layers. Squeezed by pressure, it shoots up on its own when drilled, creating an artesian well!
copy.tl: May groundwater na nakulong sa confined aquifer sa pagitan ng masikip na bato. Dahil sa presyon, kusang sumisirit ito pataas kapag binutasan, na ginagawa itong artesian well!
copy.bis: Adunay groundwater nga nabilanggo sa confined aquifer tunga sa sikit nga bato. Tungod sa presyon, mogawas kini nga mag-isa kung tusokon, nga gihimong artesian well!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Groundwater slowly dissolves soft rock like limestone
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate how erosion transports Earth materials
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes chemical weathering (dissolution of limestone by groundwater) forming caves, not erosion transporting Earth materials. It does not demonstrate transport of materials by erosion.

copy.en:
How are big underground caves made?

Groundwater slowly dissolves soft rock like limestone over long ages, carving out large caves underground!
copy.tl:
Paano nabubuo ang malalaking kuweba?

Dahan-dahang tinutunaw ng groundwater ang malambot na bato gaya ng limestone, na nakakaukit ng malalaking kuweba!
copy.bis:
Giunsa paghimo sa dagkong langob?

Hinay-hinay nga gitunaw sa groundwater ang humok nga bato sama sa limestone, nga nagukit og dagkong langob!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the female lions — the lionesses — who do most of the hunting
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to group animals according to the food they eat: plant eaters (herbivores), meat eaters (carnivores), and plant and meat-eaters (omnivores)
assignedReviews.reason: The card states that lionesses do most of the hunting, but it does not group lions by diet or classify them as herbivores, carnivores, or omnivores. Hunting behavior is only loosely related to carnivorous diet classification.

assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions hunting as a food-gathering activity but does not describe any outer body parts of animals or their roles in movement and food gathering. It provides no direct support for observing or describing body parts.

copy.en: In a lion pride, it's the female lions — the lionesses — who do most of the hunting.
copy.tl: Sa isang pride ng leon, ang mga babaeng leon o lioness ang gumagawa ng karamihan ng pangangaso.
copy.bis: Sa usa ka pride sa leon, ang baye nga mga leon o lioness ang naghimo sa kadaghanan sa pagpangayam.

copy.en: The grouper (lapu-lapu) is often found near the sea bottom, hiding among rocks and caves.
copy.tl: Ang lapu-lapu ay madalas matagpuan sa ilalim ng dagat, nagtatago sa mga bato at kweba.
copy.bis: Ang lapu-lapu kasagaran makit-an sa ilawom sa dagat, nagtago sa mga bato ug langob.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The human brain grows fastest in the first three years of life
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: compare the life cycles of mammals from birth to adulthood, birds from egg to a mature organism, and plants from seed to a young plant, and then to a mature plant
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses human brain growth in early childhood, which is a developmental fact about a mammal, but it does not compare life cycles of mammals, birds, or plants as required by the competency. copy.en:
When does the human brain grow fastest?

The human brain grows fastest in the first three years of life, forming millions of nerve connections every second — the foundation for all future learning.
copy.tl:
Kailan pinakamabilis lumaki ang utak ng tao?

Pinakamabilis lumaki ang utak ng tao sa unang tatlong taon ng buhay, na bumubuo ng milyun-milyong koneksyon ng nerve bawat segundo — ang pundasyon ng lahat ng pagkatuto sa hinaharap.
copy.bis:
Kanus-a pinakadali motubo ang utok sa tawo?

Pinakadali motubo ang utok sa tawo sa unang tulo ka tuig sa kinabuhi, nga nagporma og milyon-milyon nga koneksyon sa nerbyo matag segundo — ang pundasyon sa tanang pagkatuto sa umaabot.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Boiled guava leaves make a wash used for cleaning wounds and skin.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the root and shoot system in plants and describe why they are important
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions leaves (part of the shoot system) but does not describe the root and shoot system or why they are important to the plant. It focuses on a human medicinal use of leaves, not plant structure or function.

copy.en: Boiled guava leaves make a wash used for cleaning wounds and skin.
copy.tl: Pinakukuluan ang dahon ng bayabas para gawing panghugas ng sugat at pampalinis ng balat.
copy.bis: Ang dahon sa bayabas ginabukal aron himuong panghugas sa samad ug panglimpyo sa panit.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A guava is green when unripe, and it turns yellowish when it's ready to eat.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A guava is green when unripe, and it turns yellowish when it's ready to eat.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: compare the life cycles of mammals from birth to adulthood, birds from egg to a mature organism, and plants from seed to a young plant, and then to a mature plant
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a single stage change (unripe to ripe) in a fruit, but does not compare life cycles from seed to young plant to mature plant. It does not provide the developmental stages or comparison required by the competency.

copy.en:
How do you know a guava is ripe?

A guava is green when unripe, and it turns yellowish when it's ready to eat.
copy.tl:
Paano malalaman kung hinog na ang bayabas?

Berde ang bayabas kapag hilaw pa, at nagiging madilaw-dilaw kapag hinog na.
copy.bis:
Unsaon pagkahibalo nga hinog na ang bayabas?

Berde ang bayabas kung hilaw pa, ug mahimong dilaw-dilaw kung hinog na.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It sets into a yummy jelly when it is boiled in water and then cooled.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how changes in temperature cause matter to change in state, such as solid to liquid to gas
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes agar setting into a jelly when boiled and cooled, which is a sol-gel transition, not a change of state among solid, liquid, and gas as required by the competency. It does not teach melting, evaporation, freezing, or condensation, so it only shares the broad theme of temperature affecting matter.

copy.en: Gulaman is made from agar taken from seaweed! It sets into a yummy jelly when it is boiled in water and then cooled.
copy.tl: Ang gulaman ay gawa sa agar na kinukuha mula sa damong-dagat! Namumuo itong parang jelly kapag pinakuluan sa tubig at saka pinalamig.
copy.bis: Ang gulaman gihimo gikan sa agar nga gikuha sa damong-dagat! Mogahi kini nga morag jelly kon lutoon sa tubig ug human pabugnawon.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Gumamela leaves are shiny and green, with edges that look just like tiny teeth!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the outer parts of plants, such as leaves, roots, and stems and identify their role to get water and nutrients from the soil
assignedReviews.reason: The card only describes the appearance of gumamela leaves (shiny, green, toothed edges). It does not address the role of leaves in getting water and nutrients from the soil, which is the core action of the competency. The shared topic of 'leaves' is not enough for direct support.

copy.en: Gumamela leaves are shiny and green, with edges that look just like tiny teeth!
copy.tl: Ang mga dahon ng gumamela ay makintab at berde, may gilid na parang maliliit na ngipin!
copy.bis: Ang mga dahon sa gumamela masinaw ug berde, adunay daplin nga morag gagmay nga ngipon!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: In santan the stamens stay separate, but in gumamela they're joined into one long tube
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a table to show how living things can be classified into groups based on similar characteristics (plants including flowering and non-flowering; animals including mammals, reptiles, insects, birds, fish, amphibians; microorganisms including fungi and bacteria)

copy.en:
How can you tell a gumamela apart?

In santan the stamens stay separate, but in gumamela they're joined into one long tube — an easy way to spot it!
copy.tl:
Paano makikilala kaagad ang gumamela?

Sa santan, hiwa-hiwalay ang mga stamen, pero sa gumamela pinagsama ang mga ito sa isang mahabang tubo — madaling paraan para makilala ito!
copy.bis:
Unsaon pag-ila dayon sa gumamela?

Sa santan, bulag-bulag ang mga stamen, apan sa gumamela gitapok kini sa usa ka taas nga tubo — sayon nga paagi aron mailhan kini!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the pistil travels up through the stamen tube and pokes out at the very tip
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the outer parts of plants, such as leaves, roots, and stems and identify their role to get water and nutrients from the soil
assignedReviews.reason: Pistil arrangement inside a stamen tube is not leaves, roots, or stems taking water and nutrients from soil.

assignedReviews.reason: Pistil/stamen geometry is adjacent to sexual reproduction; the card never describes pollination, seed production, or propagation.

copy.en:
Why can you see red tips above a gumamela's tube?

Inside a gumamela flower, the pistil travels up through the stamen tube and pokes out at the very tip — that's the red bit you see!
copy.tl:
Bakit may pulang dulo sa itaas ng tubo ng gumamela?

Sa gumamela, dumadaan ang pistil sa loob ng tubo ng stamen at lumalabas sa dulo nito. Kaya kitang-kita ang pulang dulo ng pistil sa itaas ng tubo.
copy.bis:
Nganong naay pula nga tumoy ibabaw sa tubo sa gumamela?

Sa gumamela, moagi ang pistil sa sulod sa tubo sa stamen ug mogula sa tumoy niini. Mao nga makita nimo ang pula nga tumoy sa pistil ibabaw sa tubo.

assignedReviews.reason: The card only lists the three ingredients of gunpowder. It does not describe gunpowder as a mixture, nor does it address uniform vs non-uniform mixtures, solutions, or suspensions. The content is only tangentially related to mixtures.

copy.en:
What three ingredients make up gunpowder?

Did you know gunpowder is made from just three ingredients: sulfur, saltpeter, and charcoal?
copy.tl:
Anong tatlong sangkap ang gumagawa ng gunpowder?

Alam mo bang ang gunpowder ay gawa sa tatlong sangkap: sulfur (asupre), saltpeter, at charcoal (uling)?
copy.bis:
Unsa nga tulo ka sangkap ang naghimo sa gunpowder?

Nahibaw-an ba nimo nga ang gunpowder gihimo gikan sa tulo ka sangkap: sulfur, saltpeter, ug charcoal (uling)?

copy.bis: Ang imong bituka puy-anan sa bilyun-bilyong maayong bacteria nga nagtabang sa pagtunaw sa pagkaon ug nanalipod kanimo batok sa makadaot nga mga mikrobyo.

copy.tl: Kapag pinaghihiwa-hiwalay ng bakterya ang hibla, gumagawa sila ng acid na nagpapakain at nagpapalusog sa mga selula ng bituka mo!
copy.bis: Kon bungkagon sa bakterya ang lanot, naghimo sila og mga asido nga makapakaon ug makapahimsog sa mga selula sa imong tinai!

How do leaf-eating animals digest tough leaves?

Oo! Napakaliit ng mga germ kaya hindi ito nakikita — puwede pa ring puno ng mikrobyo ang kamay kahit walang nakikitang dumi. Hugasan pa rin!

Kinahanglan pa bang hugasan ang morag limpyo nga kamot?

Oo! Gagmay kaayo ang mga germ nga dili makita — puno gihapon og mikrobyo ang kamot bisan walay makita nga hugaw. Hugasi gihapon!

Naggikan kini sa Griyego nga pulong helios, nga nagpasabot og adlaw!

Ano ang pinakamalakas na kalamnan ng katawan?

Ang kalamnan ng panga (masseter) ang itinuturing na pinakamalakas na kalamnan sa katawan batay sa lakas nitong ipinupuwersa kapag kumakagat.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang pinakakusgan nga unod sa lawas?

Ang unod sa apapangig (masseter) giisip nga pinakakusgan nga unod sa lawas base sa kusog nga mahatag niini kung mopaak.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: An adult human body has 206 bones in total!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card states the number of bones in an adult human body, which is a fact about the skeletal system, but it does not describe how the skeletal system (or any other body system) works. copy.en:
How many bones do adults have?

An adult human body has 206 bones in total!
copy.tl:
Ilang buto ang mayroon ang adult?

Ang katawan ng isang adultong tao ay may 206 na buto!
copy.bis:
Pila ka bukog ang naa sa hamtong?

Ang lawas sa usa ka hamtong nga tawo adunay 206 ka bukog!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: On average, people around the world live to about 73 years old.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: compare the life cycles of mammals from birth to adulthood, birds from egg to a mature organism, and plants from seed to a young plant, and then to a mature plant
assignedReviews.reason: The card states a single average human lifespan figure. It does not compare life cycles of mammals, birds, or plants, nor describe stages from birth/egg/seed to maturity. The content is only tangentially related to living things and does not support the competency's comparative life-cycle skill.

copy.en: On average, people around the world live to about 73 years old.
copy.tl: Karaniwang umaabot ang tao sa buong mundo sa mga 73 taong gulang.
copy.bis: Kasagaran ang tawo sa tibuok kalibutan moabot og mga 73 ka tuig ang panuigon.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A human baby grows inside its mother for about 9 months before it's born.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify which groups of animals reproduce by giving birth to live young, such as mammals, and which reproduce by laying eggs, such as birds and reptiles
assignedReviews.reason: The card states a fact about human pregnancy duration but does not teach the classification of animals into live-bearing (mammals) vs egg-laying (birds, reptiles) groups. It provides no contrast or group identification, so it does not directly support the competency.

copy.en: A human baby grows inside its mother for about 9 months before it's born.
copy.tl: Umaabot ng mga 9 na buwan bago isilang ang isang sanggol sa loob ng katawan ng kanyang ina.
copy.bis: Mokabat og mga 9 ka bulan sa dili pa matawo ang usa ka masuso sa sulod sa lawas sa iyang inahan.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The scientific name of humans is Homo sapiens
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain why humans are classified under Class Mammalia and the Order Primates

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The scientific name of humans is Homo sapiens
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a table to show how living things can be classified into groups based on similar characteristics (plants including flowering and non-flowering; animals including mammals, reptiles, insects, birds, fish, amphibians; microorganisms including fungi and bacteria)
assignedReviews.reason: The card gives a scientific name but does not use a table or classify living things into the named groups such as mammals, reptiles, insects, etc. It is only tangentially related to classification.

copy.en:
What is the scientific name of humans?

The scientific name of humans is Homo sapiens — Homo is the genus, and sapiens is the species.
copy.tl:
Ano ang siyentipikong pangalan ng tao?

Ang siyentipikong pangalan ng tao ay Homo sapiens — ang Homo ang genus at ang sapiens ang species.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang siyentipiko nga ngalan sa tawo?

Ang siyentipiko nga ngalan sa tawo mao ang Homo sapiens — ang Homo mao ang genus ug ang sapiens mao ang species.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: a hummingbird also eats tiny insects to get protein
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to group animals according to the food they eat: plant eaters (herbivores), meat eaters (carnivores), and plant and meat-eaters (omnivores)
assignedReviews.reason: The card states a dietary fact (hummingbird eats nectar and insects) but does not group animals into herbivore/carnivore/omnivore categories or use secondary sources. assignedReviews.card_evidence: a hummingbird also eats tiny insects to get protein
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: draw a simple food chain using living things from the Philippines and label them as herbivores, carnivores, and omnivores
assignedReviews.reason: The competency requires drawing a food chain of Philippine living things labeled with trophic roles. The card mentions a hummingbird's diet but does not present a food chain, label roles, or use Philippine-specific organisms. It is only tangentially related to food chains.

copy.en: Besides nectar, a hummingbird also eats tiny insects to get protein.
copy.tl: Bukod sa nektar, kumakain din ang hummingbird ng maliliit na insekto para magkaroon ng protina.
copy.bis: Gawas sa nektar, ang hummingbird mokaon usab og gagmayng insekto aron makakuha og protina.

copy.en:
What's the smallest bird in the world?

The bee hummingbird is the smallest bird in the world, only about 5 centimeters long.
copy.tl:
Ano ang pinakamaliit na ibon sa mundo?

Ang bee hummingbird ang pinakamaliit na ibon sa mundo, halos 5 sentimetro lang ang haba.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang pinakagamay nga langgam sa kalibutan?

Ang bee hummingbird mao ang pinakagamay nga langgam sa kalibutan, mga 5 sentimetro ra ang gitas-on.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: This dark part of the soil is made from decayed leaves and animals that give it nutrients
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how soil is formed from rocks and minerals
assignedReviews.reason: Humus from decayed leaves is not how soil is formed from rocks and minerals.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: This dark part of the soil is made from decayed leaves and animals that give it nutrients
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the roles of producers, consumers, scavengers, and decomposers in a food web
assignedReviews.reason: Humus as decayed matter is not the roles of producers, consumers, scavengers, and decomposers in a food web.

copy.en:
What gives soil its dark color and nutrients?

It's humus! This dark part of the soil is made from decayed leaves and animals that give it nutrients.
copy.tl:
Ano ang nagbibigay ng madilim na kulay at sustansya sa lupa?

Ang humus! Ito yung madilim na bahagi ng lupa na gawa sa mga bulok na dahon at hayop na nagbibigay sustansya.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang naghatag og itom nga kolor ug sustansya sa yuta?

Ang humus! Kini mao ang itom nga bahin sa yuta nga gikan sa nadunot nga dahon ug hayop nga naghatag og sustansya.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Your brain — especially a part called the hypothalamus — sends the signals that make you feel hungry.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe homeostasis as a state of balance among all the body systems in humans that needs to be maintained for survival and proper functioning; its indicators include body temperature, glucose level, and blood pressure
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states that the hypothalamus sends hunger signals. Hunger is tangentially related to homeostasis but the card does not directly support the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Your brain — especially a part called the hypothalamus — sends the signals that make you feel hungry.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use models, flow charts, diagrams, and simulations to explain how body systems work together, such as digestion and excretion
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a brain function but does not use models, flow charts, diagrams, or simulations, and does not explain how body systems work together (e.g., digestion and excretion). It only identifies a single brain region's role in hunger, which is not direct support for the competency.

copy.en:
What part of your brain makes you feel hungry?

Your brain — especially a part called the hypothalamus — sends the signals that make you feel hungry.
copy.tl:
Anong bahagi ng utak ang nagpapadama ng gutom?

Ang iyong utak, lalo na ang bahaging tinatawag na hypothalamus, ang nagpapadala ng senyales na nagpapadama sa iyong gutom.
copy.bis:
Unsang bahin sa utok ang nagpabati og gutom?

Ang imong utok, ilabi na ang bahin nga gitawag og hypothalamus, mao ang nagpadala sa senyales nga nagpabati kanimo og gutom.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: rice with viand is the meal that chases away hunger and gives kids energy
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the basic needs of all living things, such as air, food, water, and shelter
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes rice as a food that relieves hunger and provides energy, but it does not teach the concept of basic needs (air, food, water, shelter) or ask students to identify them. It only gives a specific example of food without connecting it to the general category of basic needs.

copy.en: In the Philippines, rice with viand is the meal that chases away hunger and gives kids energy to play and study.
copy.tl: Sa Pilipinas, ang kanin at ulam ang pagkaing nag-aalis ng gutom at nagbibigay-lakas sa mga bata para maglaro at mag-aral.
copy.bis: Sa Pilipinas, ang kan-on ug sud-an ang pagkaon nga nagtangtang sa gutom ug maghatag kusog sa mga bata para modula ug motuon.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Hydrogen fuel cells convert the chemical energy of hydrogen and oxygen into electricity.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how important types of chemical reactions, such as combustion, acids on metals, acids on carbonates, photosynthesis, and respiration, relate to or impact the natural and built environments using information from secondary sources
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a chemical reaction (hydrogen + oxygen → water) but not one of the listed important types (combustion, acids on metals, acids on carbonates, photosynthesis, respiration). It does not explain how the reaction impacts natural or built environments beyond a general clean-energy claim, and no secondary sources are used.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: making it a clean energy technology with no carbon dioxide!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: gather information from secondary sources to evaluate how renewable and non-renewable generation of electricity in the Philippines impacts human activities and the environment
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions clean energy and no carbon dioxide, which touches on environmental impact of electricity generation, but it does not evaluate renewable/non-renewable generation in the Philippines or gather information from secondary sources. The focus is on hydrogen fuel cells, not the required evaluation of Philippine electricity generation.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: convert the chemical energy of hydrogen and oxygen into electricity
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that energy is something that can cause change including light, sound, and heat energy
assignedReviews.reason: The card shows chemical energy being converted to electricity, which is a form of energy causing change, but the competency specifically requires identifying energy as something that can cause change including light, sound, and heat energy. The card does not address light, sound, or heat, and is at a much higher grade level.

copy.en: Hydrogen fuel cells convert the chemical energy of hydrogen and oxygen into electricity. Water is the only byproduct, making it a clean energy technology with no carbon dioxide!
copy.tl: Ang hydrogen fuel cells ay nagko-convert ng chemical energy ng hydrogen at oxygen sa electricity. Tubig lang ang byproduct, kaya ito ay malinis na energy technology na walang carbon dioxide!
copy.bis: Ang hydrogen fuel cells nagconvert sa chemical energy sa hydrogen ug oxygen ngadto sa electricity. Tubig ra ang byproduct, mao nga kini malinis nga energy technology nga walay carbon dioxide!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The scientist Antoine Lavoisier gave hydrogen its very cool name
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to identify a famous Filipino and/or foreign scientist and their invention/s
assignedReviews.reason: The card identifies a famous foreign scientist (Lavoisier) but describes his naming of hydrogen, not an invention. The competency specifically requires identifying a scientist and their invention/s. Naming a substance is not an invention, so the card does not directly support the stated skill.

copy.en: The scientist Antoine Lavoisier gave hydrogen its very cool name, which actually means water-former in English!
copy.tl: Si Antoine Lavoisier ang nagbigay ng magandang pangalang hydrogen, na ang ibig sabihin ay 'gumagawa ng tubig'!
copy.bis: Si Antoine Lavoisier ang naghatag sa nindot nga ngalang hydrogen, nga nagpasabot og 'maghimo og tubig'!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: An ice box has thick walls that block outside heat so the ice and food inside stay cold!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify advantageous and disadvantageous examples of conduction, convection, and radiation
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes insulation blocking outside heat but does not identify or distinguish conduction, convection, or radiation, nor give advantageous/disadvantageous examples of these specific heat transfer modes.

copy.en:
How does an ice box keep your snacks chilly?

An ice box has thick walls that block outside heat so the ice and food inside stay cold!
copy.tl:
Paano pinapanatili ng ice box na malamig ang mga meryenda mo?

Ang ice box ay may makapal na dingding na pumipigil sa init mula sa labas para manatiling malamig ang yelo at pagkain sa loob!
copy.bis:
Unsaon pagpabilin sa ice box nga bugnaw ang imong mga meryenda?

Ang ice box adunay baga nga bongbong nga magpugong sa kainit gikan sa gawas aron magpabilin nga bugnaw ang yelo ug pagkaon sa sulod!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Ice floats on water because it is less dense (lighter) than liquid water.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the properties of solids, liquids, and gases in terms of shape and volume (solids: definite shape and volume; liquids: no definite shape, definite volume; gases: no definite shape or volume)
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions ice as a solid and liquid water, but it does not describe the properties of solids, liquids, and gases in terms of shape and volume. Density is not the shape/volume property targeted by this competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Ice floats on water because it is less dense (lighter) than liquid water.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Ice floats on water because it is less dense (lighter) than liquid water.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe changes of state for solids, liquids, and gases as melting, evaporation, freezing, condensation using diagrams and flowcharts
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains density and floating; it does not describe melting, evaporation, freezing, or condensation, and it does not use diagrams or flowcharts. This is not a change-of-state competency.

copy.en: Ice floats on water because it is less dense (lighter) than liquid water. That is why ice cubes bob around in your glass!
copy.tl: Lumulutang ang yelo sa tubig dahil mas magaan (mas mababa ang density) ito kaysa sa likidong tubig. Kaya lumulutang ang yelo sa iyong baso!
copy.bis: Molutaw ang yelo sa tubig kay mas gaan (mas ubos ang density) kini kaysa likidong tubig. Mao nga molutaw ang yelo sa imong baso!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the Sun delivers heat that people and living things use every day
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: make suggestions about the importance of the Sun to living things for a group or class discussion and confirm and record ideas by referring to trustworthy secondary sources
assignedReviews.reason: The card states that the Sun delivers heat used by living things, which touches on the importance of the Sun, but it does not involve making suggestions, group/class discussion, or confirming and recording ideas from trustworthy secondary sources as required by the competency.

copy.en:
Why does ice melt faster outside?

Ice in sunlight melts faster than ice in shade! This simple home test shows the Sun delivers heat that people and living things use every day.
copy.tl:
Bakit mas mabilis matunaw ang ice sa labas?

Ang ice sa sunlight ay mas mabilis matunaw kaysa sa shade! Patunay ito na ang Sun ay nagbibigay ng heat na ginagamit natin araw-araw.
copy.bis:
Ngano mas dali matunaw ang ice sa gawas?

Ang ice sa sunlight mas dali matunaw kaysa sa shade! Nagpamatuod kini nga ang Sun naghatag ug heat nga gigamit nato matag adlaw.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Most of an iceberg is hidden underwater!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore and describe things that affect the movement of objects, including size, shape, heaviness, material, and surface texture
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes an iceberg floating in water, but does not discuss movement of objects or any factors (size, shape, heaviness, material, surface texture) that affect movement. It is about buoyancy/density, not motion.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Most of an iceberg is hidden underwater!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that matter has (exists in) three states called solids, liquids, and gases
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions ice and water, which are solid and liquid states, but it does not identify that matter exists in three states (solid, liquid, gas) or teach the concept of states of matter. It only implicitly involves ice and water without naming states.

copy.en: Most of an iceberg is hidden underwater! We only see the small tip above the surface.
copy.tl: Karamihan ng iceberg ay nakatago sa ilalim ng tubig! Dulo lang nito ang nakikita natin sa ibabaw.
copy.bis: Kadaghanan sa iceberg natago sa ilawom sa tubig! Gamay lang nga tumoy ang atong makita sa ibabaw.

assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a life-cycle stage of an eel but does not use a flow chart or compare stages of animals such as butterfly, frog, chicken, or human. Format-required competency is not met, so at most related_only.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: it gets a new name: elver, or young eel!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: compare the life cycles of mammals from birth to adulthood, birds from egg to a mature organism, and plants from seed to a young plant, and then to a mature plant
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes one transition in an eel's life, but the competency requires comparing life cycles of mammals, birds, and plants from birth/egg/seed to maturity. No such comparison is present, and the eel is not one of the specified groups.

copy.en: When a see-through glass eel gains color in the river, it gets a new name: elver, or young eel!
copy.tl: Kapag nagkakulay na ang glass eel sa ilog, tinatawag na itong elver o batang igat!
copy.bis: Kung makakolor na ang glass eel sa suba, gitawag na kini nga elver o batan-ong kasili!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Most eels spawn only once, in the deep ocean, and then they die.

assignedReviews.reason: The card states that eels lay eggs (spawn) but does not identify groups of animals that give birth vs. lay eggs, nor does it classify eels among such groups. It is a specific fact about eel reproduction, not instruction on the competency's grouping skill.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Most eels spawn only once, in the deep ocean, and then they die.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use flow charts to compare the different stages in the life cycle of animals, such as a butterfly, frog, chicken, and human
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a life-cycle event (spawning) but does not use a flow chart to compare stages of a life cycle, nor does it cover the stages of any animal's life cycle. The format-required flow chart is absent, so it cannot directly support this competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Most eels spawn only once, in the deep ocean, and then they die.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce
assignedReviews.reason: The card touches on reproduction (spawning) as a characteristic of living things, but it does not describe the general characteristics of living things (grow, respond, reproduce) or provide a broader explanation. It is a single example, not direct instruction on the competency.

copy.en:
How many times does an eel lay eggs?

Most eels spawn only once, in the deep ocean, and then they die.
copy.tl:
Ilang beses lang nangingitlog ang igat?

Karaniwang nangingitlog nang minsan lamang ang igat sa kalaliman ng dagat, pagkatapos ay namamatay na ito.
copy.bis:
Pila lang ka higayon mangitlog ang kasili?

Kasagaran mangitlog lang kausa ang kasili sa lawom nga dagat, ug pagkahuman mamatay na kini.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Intrusive igneous rocks like granite cool slowly underground and grow large crystals. Extrusive rocks like basalt cool quickly at the surface and have small crystals!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore the school grounds or the local area to observe or collect different types of rocks, describing their similarities and differences in terms of features, such as texture, color, and grain crystal size
assignedReviews.reason: The card teaches a specific classification of igneous rocks (intrusive vs extrusive) and their crystal sizes, but the competency requires students to explore school grounds or the local area to observe or collect different types of rocks and describe similarities/differences in features such as texture, color, and grain crystal size. copy.en: Intrusive igneous rocks like granite cool slowly underground and grow large crystals. Extrusive rocks like basalt cool quickly at the surface and have small crystals!
copy.tl: Ang intrusive igneous rocks tulad ng granite ay pabagal na lumalamig sa ilalim ng lupa at may malalaking kristal. Ang extrusive rocks tulad ng basalt ay mabilis na lumalamig sa ibabaw at may maliliit na kristal!
copy.bis: Ang intrusive igneous rocks sama sa granite hinay ang pagkabugnaw ilalom sa yuta ug may dagkong kristal. Ang extrusive rocks sama sa basalt paspas ang pagkabugnaw sa ibabaw ug may gamay nga kristal!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the water acts just like a mirror, reflecting the beautiful images of everything above it
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: carry out guided investigations to describe and illustrate the reflection of light using plane and curved mirrors and the refraction of light using transparent blocks, lenses, and prisms with examples from everyday applications
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states that calm water reflects images like a mirror. It does not involve guided investigations, does not address plane or curved mirrors, and does not cover refraction with transparent blocks, lenses, or prisms. It shares the topic of reflection but provides no direct instructional support for the competency's required activities or equipment.

copy.en: When a lake or sea is perfectly calm, the water acts just like a mirror, reflecting the beautiful images of everything above it!
copy.tl: Kapag tahimik ang lawa o dagat, ang tubig ay kumikilos tulad ng salamin, na nagpapakita ng mga imahe ng mga bagay sa ibabaw nito!
copy.bis: Kung hinay ang tubig sa danaw o dagat, ang tubig naglihok sama sa salamin, nagpakita sa mga hulagway sa mga butang sa ibabaw niini!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: your body sometimes heats itself up as a fever
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe homeostasis as a state of balance among all the body systems in humans that needs to be maintained for survival and proper functioning; its indicators include body temperature, glucose level, and blood pressure
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions body temperature, which is one indicator of homeostasis, but it does not describe homeostasis as a state of balance among body systems or explain how it is maintained. It only presents fever as a defensive response, not the concept of homeostasis itself.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: your body sometimes heats itself up as a fever
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a response of the body to germs, which could be seen as 'respond', but it does not teach the general characteristics of living things (grow, respond, reproduce). It is a specific immune response, not a lesson on the characteristics of living things.

copy.en:
Why do you get a fever when sick?

When germs invade, your body sometimes heats itself up as a fever. The extra heat can slow down some germs while your immune system fights them off.
copy.tl:
Bakit tayo nilalagnat kapag may sakit?

Kapag may impeksyon, minsan iniinit ng katawan ang sarili bilang lagnat. Ang init na ito ay nakakapagpabagal sa ilang germ habang lumalaban ang immune system.
copy.bis:
Ngano nagahilanat ta kon masakit?

Kon adunay impeksyon, usahay ginapainit sa lawas ang kaugalingon isip hilanat. Kining init makapahinay sa pipila ka germ samtang nagpakig-away ang immune system.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the Department of Health runs a free vaccine program at health centers and barangays, following a schedule so every child gets protected against common diseases.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from the home or the local community to identify a science invention and explain its impact on their everyday life
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a public health program (free vaccines) but does not identify a specific science invention or explain its impact on everyday life. Vaccines are inventions, but the card focuses on the program's schedule and availability, not on the invention itself or its mechanism/impact. This is only tangentially related to the competency.

copy.en: In the Philippines, the Department of Health runs a free vaccine program at health centers and barangays, following a schedule so every child gets protected against common diseases.
copy.tl: Sa Pilipinas, may libreng programa ng bakuna sa mga health center at barangay na pinapatakbo ng Department of Health, may iskedyul para maprotektahan ang bawat bata laban sa karaniwang sakit.
copy.bis: Sa Pilipinas, adunay libreng programa sa bakuna sa mga health center ug barangay nga gipadagan sa Department of Health, adunay iskedyul aron mapanalipdan ang matag bata batok sa kasagarang sakit.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: To make some vaccines, scientists weaken or kill the germ in a lab until it can't cause disease anymore
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to identify examples of modern biotechnology, such as genetically modified organisms and processes (e.g. in vitro fertilization)
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a vaccine production process, which is a biotechnology application, but it does not identify examples of modern biotechnology such as GMOs or in vitro fertilization, nor does it frame the content as an example of modern biotechnology. It only provides background on how vaccines are made, so it does not directly support the competency's skill of identifying examples of modern biotechnology.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: To make some vaccines, scientists weaken or kill the germ in a lab until it can't cause disease anymore
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: recognize that some organisms consist of a single cell (unicellular) like in bacteria and some consist of many cells (multicellular) like in a human
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses weakening germs for vaccines and has no connection to unicellular vs. multicellular organisms. It does not mention bacteria, single cells, or multicellularity, so it is unrelated to the competency.

copy.en: To make some vaccines, scientists weaken or kill the germ in a lab until it can't cause disease anymore, using just enough for the body to safely learn to recognize it.
copy.tl: Para makagawa ng ilang bakuna, pinahihina o pinapatay ng mga siyentista ang germ sa laboratoryo hanggang hindi na ito makapagdulot ng sakit, gamit lang ang sapat na bahagi para makilala ito ng katawan nang ligtas.

copy.en:
How do geologists know the exact temperature and pressure a rock experienced?

They check index minerals! Minerals like chlorite (low grade) and sillimanite (very high grade) reveal the exact heat and pressure a metamorphic rock faced.
copy.tl:
Paano nalalaman ng mga geologist ang eksaktong temperatura at presyon na naranasan ng isang bato?

Tinitingnan nila ang index minerals! Ang mga mineral tulad ng chlorite (mababang grade) at sillimanite (napakataas na grade) ay nagpapakita ng init at presyon na naranasan ng metamorphic rock.
copy.bis:
Unsaon pagkahibalo sa mga geologist sa eksaktong temperatura ug presyon nga nasinati sa bato?

Gitan-aw nila ang index minerals! Ang mga mineral sama sa chlorite (ubos nga grade) ug sillimanite (labing taas nga grade) nagpakita sa init ug presyon nga nasinati sa metamorphic rock.
